interpretations: Group by `orders.timespan`, using an inner join of `riskandmargin` to `orders` on `ordervault = recordvault`. Show each time in force, its count of matched risk/margin records, the share (count ÷ total matched records), and the difference between that share and the average share across time-in-force values (1 ÷ number of distinct time-in-force values). The difference is signed, with no rounding
Same as 1, but the difference is an absolute value (the magnitude of the deviation)
Same as 1, but the average share is the mean of the per-group shares, computed with AVG over the grouped shares. This equals 1 ÷ the number of groups, and it is the same as interpretation 1 in value
Same as 1, but the share is expressed as a percentage (×100), and the deviation from the average share is in percentage points
Same as 1, but the count is the number of distinct `riskandmargin.riskandmarginpivot` values per time in force, rather than the number of rows
Same as 1, but the count is the number of distinct orders (`orders.recordvault`) that have risk/margin records, per time in force
Same as 1, but the count excludes records whose `risk_margin_profile` is NULL
Same as 1, but time-in-force values with no matched risk/margin records are also listed, with a count of 0. The average share then includes those values
Same as 1, but orders with a NULL `timespan` form their own group, and that group is included in the average-share denominator
Same as 1, but orders with a NULL `timespan` are excluded from the groups, the total and the average
The share is calculated against the total number of all risk/margin records, including unmatched ones. The average share is across the time-in-force groups
The deviation is expressed as a ratio relative to the average share, (share − average share) ÷ average share, instead of a raw difference
The average share is the overall share ÷ the number of time-in-force values, where the number of values comes from all enum values (GTC, IOC, GTD, FOK), even if absent from the data
The "time in force" is read from a time-in-force field inside `risk_margin_profile` rather than from `orders.timespan`
queries:
SELECT
  o.timespan AS timespan,
  COUNT(*) AS record_count,
  CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM riskandmargin r2 JOIN orders o2 ON r2.ordervault = o2.recordvault) AS share,
  CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM riskandmargin r2 JOIN orders o2 ON r2.ordervault = o2.recordvault)
    - 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o3.timespan) FROM riskandmargin r3 JOIN orders o3 ON r3.ordervault = o3.recordvault) AS share_diff
FROM riskandmargin r
JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
GROUP BY o.timespan;
SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share
FROM (
  SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders) AS share
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY ordertune
);
WITH s AS (
  SELECT exchspot, 100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share_pct
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY exchspot
)
SELECT exchspot, share_pct, share_pct - AVG(share_pct) OVER () AS deviation_pp
FROM s;
SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(DISTINCT r.riskandmarginpivot) AS count
FROM orders o
JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
GROUP BY o.timespan;
SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
FROM orders o
JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
GROUP BY o.timespan
